name: Pedal Box & Brake Bias
description: Driver input end of the brake system. Factory: GM hanging pedal bracket pushing a vacuum booster. Race: floor-mount pedal box with a threaded balance bar splitting pedal force between separate front and rear master cylinders, adjustable from the cockpit by a remote cable.

components.name: Brake pedal assembly (pedal box)
components.description: Holds the brake (and clutch/throttle) pedals and reacts the full pedal load (race drivers can exceed 100–150 lbf at the pad, ~1,000+ lbf at the master-cylinder pushrod with a 5–6:1 ratio). On a bare-shell build the floor-mount race box is the norm because it puts the master cylinders inside the cockpit, removes the booster, and lets you set pedal ratio and bias.
components.location: Driver footwell, bolted to the floor pan / a reinforcing plate tied to the cage, pedal pads at x≈0.85–0.95, z≈+0.30–0.45. Factory unit hangs from the dash/cowl structure and pushes through the firewall into the booster.

factory.name: GM Gen 6 Camaro hanging brake pedal bracket (manual-trans cars share the bracket with the clutch pedal)
factory.notes: Steel stamped bracket; pedal pushrod feeds the vacuum booster through the firewall. Retained by studs/nuts at the dash panel. Brake pedal position (BPP) sensor on the bracket feeds ECM/EBCM/brake lights.

raceOptions.name: Tilton 800/900-Series floor-mount pedal assembly
raceOptions.notes: Tilton states its 78-Series master cylinders fit 800- and 900-Series pedal assemblies. Forward- or reverse-mount, adjustable ratio, integral balance bar.

raceOptions.name: Tilton 600-Series floor-mount pedal assembly
raceOptions.notes: Common in production-based race cars (dual master + clutch). Verify footwell clearance against the Gen 6 tunnel.

raceOptions.name: Wilwood Tru-Bar / Triple floor-mount pedal assembly
raceOptions.notes: Lower-cost option with balance bar and compact remote-reservoir masters.

raceOptions.name: OBP / AP Racing CP5500-series pedal box
raceOptions.notes: Alternative race pedal boxes; AP CP-series pairs with AP CP2xxx/CP7855 master cylinders.

specs.Pedal ratio (race target): 5.0–6.0 : 1 (typical race floor mount with no booster)
specs.Pedal travel to firm: Aim for firm pedal within ~1–1.5 in (25–38 mm) travel

hardware.item: Factory brake pedal assembly retaining nut (to dash panel studs)
hardware.notes: Value from GM 2016–18 SM table ("Brake pedal assembly nut"). Quantity estimated.

hardware.spec: 3/8-16 UNC or M10x1.5 bolt, nyloc nut + large washers each side
hardware.notes: Engineering value for 3/8 Grade 8 into a 3–5 mm steel plate; follow pedal box manufacturer if specified. Bolts must clamp through a doubler, never thin floor sheet alone.
Torque only until pedals pivot freely without axial play.

installNotes: Set seat position and steering column first, then position the pedal box so the brake pedal pad sits on the driver's natural foot line with heel-and-toe spacing to the throttle (throttle pedal is in the engine/interior systems).
Fabricate a 3–5 mm steel (or 6 mm aluminum) floor plate that spreads load across the floor pan and ties to the cage / footbox; weld or through-bolt with backing plates.
Set pedal ratio on the pedal (most race boxes have 2–3 pushrod hole positions). Start ~5.5:1 with 0.70/0.75 in front/rear masters, then tune.
After plumbing and bleeding, check that the pedal hits a firm stop well before the pedal stop/floor; add a positive pedal over-travel stop.
Factory pedal: torque nuts to spec, reconnect BPP sensor and confirm brake lights / EBCM see the switch.
inspection: Check pedal pivot for play and cracked welds at the floor plate each event.
Confirm pedal pad bolts tight and pedal stop not contacted under max braking.

sources.title: TightTorque – Chevrolet Camaro 6 (2016–2024) torque table, compiled from GM 2016–2018 Camaro service manual sections
Tilton Racing – 78-Series master cylinders (bores, AN3 outlet, AN6 inlet, 3/8-24 pushrod; not for ABS, use 79-Series)

images.title: Tilton 600-series pedal assemblies spec sheet (Porterfield PDF)

modelRef.dimensions: Floor-mount box ~200 x 270 mm footprint, pivot at y=0.24, pads 0.42-0.46 high
modelRef.features: Aluminium base + front MC bulkhead, common pivot shaft, 3 forged pedals (clutch / brake with balance-bar tube / throttle), black pads

components.name: Pedal box floor reinforcement plate
components.description: Steel doubler that spreads pedal box loads into the unibody floor and cage. Without it the thin factory floor flexes, giving a long, inconsistent pedal.
components.location: Driver footwell floor under the pedal box, x≈0.80–1.00, z≈+0.25–0.50.

factory.name: None (factory pedal hangs from dash structure)

raceOptions.name: Fabricated 3/16 in (4.8 mm) steel plate with gussets
raceOptions.notes: Stitch/plug weld to floor or through-bolt with backing plates; tie forward edge to the firewall and/or cage foot bars.

specs.Attachment: Plug weld or 8x M8/5/16 bolts with backing plates

hardware.spec: 5/16-18 UNC or M8x1.25, with 3 mm backing washers

installNotes: Install during chassis prep before paint and before the brake hard lines are routed.
Pre-drill master cylinder pushrod and line clearance holes in the firewall/footbox before paint.
inspection: Check for cracking at welds around plate perimeter annually.

modelRef.features: Steel plate bolted / welded to the footwell floor

components.name: Brake balance (bias) bar
components.description: Threaded bar passing through a spherical bearing in the brake pedal; each end carries a clevis to a master cylinder pushrod. Turning the bar shifts the pivot point toward one master cylinder, changing the front/rear force split mechanically (typical adjustment range ~60/40 to 40/60 of pedal force).
components.location: Across the top of the brake pedal in the pedal box, x≈0.84, y≈0.27, z≈+0.37.

factory.name: Not fitted (factory uses fixed hydraulic split + EBCM electronic brake-force distribution)
factory.notes: Gen 6 uses Dynamic Rear Proportioning/EBD in the EBCM instead of a mechanical valve.

raceOptions.name: Tilton balance bar assembly (supplied with Tilton pedal boxes)

specs.Initial setup: Center the bar so both clevises are equidistant from the pedal bearing and the bar is square to the pedal at rest; both pushrods should start moving at the same time

hardware.notes: Clevis must thread onto pushrod at least 1x diameter (≈10 mm) engagement.

hardware.item: Balance bar lock / jam nuts at the pedal bearing
hardware.torque: Snug – bar must be able to self-align in spherical bearing; leave 0.5–1 mm end clearance
hardware.notes: If too tight the bar cannot pivot and bias becomes unpredictable.

hardware.spec: 5/16 in clevis pin with R-clip or cotter pin

installNotes: With masters installed, thread both clevises equally, then set the bar so the pedal sits square at rest with ~0.5–1 mm free play before either master piston moves (masters must fully return to uncover compensating ports).
Record the baseline bias position (number of exposed threads each side) in the setup sheet.
Verify bias on track with front and rear line pressure sensors or by threshold-brake testing: rears should lock just after the fronts.
inspection: Check clevis pins, clips and jam nuts every event.
Confirm bar still free to swivel in the pedal bearing.
Note bias knob turns from baseline in log book.

sources.title: Tilton Racing – 78-Series master cylinders (bores, AN3 outlet, AN6 inlet, 3/8-24 pushrod; not for ABS, use 79-Series)

modelRef.dimensions: 3/8-24 threaded bar, ~130 mm between clevis ends
modelRef.features: Spherical bearing tube in the pedal, two clevises, adjuster end

components.name: Remote brake-bias adjuster cable & knob
components.description: Flexible push-pull/rotary cable that turns the balance bar from the cockpit so the driver can shift bias as fuel burns off and tires wear. A knob with detents (clicks) is mounted within reach on the dash or center console.
components.location: Cable from the balance bar end up under the dash to a knob on the dash or console (x≈1.1–1.2, near the steering column, driver side).

raceOptions.name: Tilton remote bias adjuster cable (various lengths)
raceOptions.notes: Match the cable end to the balance bar (square drive).

specs.Cable length: Measure routed length +10% (typically 36–48 in for a dash-mount knob)
specs.Bend radius: Minimum ~6 in (150 mm) to avoid binding

hardware.spec: Thin panel nut supplied with cable (approx. 1/2 or 5/8 in)

installNotes: Route with gentle bends, clear of steering column, throttle and pedal travel; support every 200–300 mm.
Label the knob direction (more front / more rear) and count detents per full turn.
inspection: Turn the knob full range in the paddock to confirm it moves the bar without binding.

modelRef.features: Black sheathed cable, red knurled knob

components.name: Brake light switch / brake pressure switch
components.description: Signals brake application to the brake lights and to the ECU/data system. Factory uses a brake pedal position (BPP) sensor that also feeds the EBCM. Race builds typically use a hydraulic pressure switch or (better) line-pressure transducers that drive the rain/brake light through the PDM.
components.location: Factory: on the pedal bracket. Race: teed into the rear master cylinder outlet or a brake distribution block.

factory.name: GM brake pedal position (BPP) sensor
factory.notes: Required by the factory ECM for cruise/torque management and by the EBCM; an ECU swap must still receive a brake signal for traction/launch logic.

raceOptions.name: Hydraulic brake light pressure switch, 1/8 NPT or M10x1

hardware.threadlocker: PTFE paste rated for brake fluid (no tape)

installNotes: Install in rear circuit tee or distribution block before bleeding; wire via PDM to brake light / rain light.
inspection: Confirm brake light works at each tech inspection.
